bull_bear.body:
- R&D-led product development: automotive sealants sales have grown at a CAGR of 30% over the last three years, with almost all of that growth from newly introduced products
- New products described as comparable to or more advanced than competitors' offerings - e.g. a low density underbody coating that lets the OEM cut weight and material consumption without performance loss, and a seam sealant that removes the need for a separate curing oven
- Import substitution capability: successfully developed products to replace imports from its erstwhile US-based technical partner, ND Industries, Inc.
- Long-standing customer partnerships and a 51-year operating history (founded 1975), with new customers added and new business won at existing customers in the sealants segment
- Internationally certified quality systems (ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, IATF 16949, FAMI-QS) supporting OEM qualification
- Diversified revenue-generating sources across multiple sectors with strong domestic demand, which management says mitigates macro risk to some extent
- SAP S/4HANA ERP with embedded automated controls and audit trail across data capture, accounting, consolidation and management reporting
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility and input-cost pass-through lag — The MD&A records a sharp increase in raw material prices from late Q3 onwards which cut over 2 percentage points from product and gross margins, with management stating the bottom line is under stress from elevated input costs because customers accept the necessary price increases only with a lag. Elevated crude oil prices cascade into raw material prices.
- Competition from global MNCs with larger R&D budgets and established OEM relationships — Listed as a Threat in the MD&A. Chembond's growth depends on winning and holding automotive OEM qualifications, where incumbents have deeper R&D capability and existing relationships; the Company's own answer is a higher-than-proportionate R&D spend which it calls possibly the only way to outgrow the competition.
- Price-led competition from global MNCs and local companies — Listed as a Threat in the MD&A - price-based competition in the Company's market segments comes from both multinational and domestic players, pressuring realisations in a business whose gross margin is already compressing.
- Dependence on continuous innovation and new-product introduction — The MD&A Risks & Concerns section states that growth of the performance materials and biosciences industry is driven by a need for constant innovation, which a strong R&D focus must sustain. Almost all of the sealants segment's three-year 30% sales CAGR came from newly introduced products, so a stalled pipeline directly stalls growth.
- Safety, health and environmental exposure of chemical manufacturing — The MD&A states the Company is exposed to safety, health and environmental risks given the diversity and complexity of its industry, and separately lists as a Threat that chemical manufacturing processes are subject to environmental hazards including pollution and waste management issues. Mitigation cited: frequent SHE audits, safety training across all locations and a Safety, Health and Environment Policy.
- Geopolitical and supply-chain disruption — Listed as a Threat: economic or geopolitical events such as wars can raise raw material costs or cause delivery delays that create supply chain instability, hitting margins and sales. Management explicitly cites the ongoing Middle East crisis with no clarity on how long it will last, alongside the Russia-Ukraine war.
- Cyberattack risk from industry digitization — Listed as a Threat: digitization of the industry increases the risk of cyberattacks which may lead to data loss, operational disruption and financial loss - relevant given the Company runs SAP S/4HANA as its platform for data capture, accounting, consolidation and management reporting.
- Macro-economic sensitivity - government policy, currency and commodity volatility — The MD&A states that macro-economic conditions such as government policy decisions, currency fluctuations and commodity price volatility can affect the business, partly mitigated because the Company's revenue-generating sources are diversified into various sectors with strong domestic demand.
- Pending litigation against the Company and its Directors — The Board's Report discloses one pending litigation against the Company and its Directors whose order is yet to be received, explained in the Corporate Governance section; apart from this no significant or material order impacting going-concern status was passed by regulators, courts or tribunals.

business.body: The Company manufactures specialty chemicals - high performance coatings, automotive sealants, metal treatment chemicals and engineering adhesives - supplying industrial and automotive OEM customers in India and abroad, supported by advanced manufacturing facilities, in-house R&D and internationally certified quality systems. Its subsidiary Chembond Biosciences Limited focuses on animal health and nutrition, producing enzymes, probiotics, prebiotics and nutritional products for the poultry, dairy and aqua segments from modern fermentation and manufacturing facilities. The Company is listed on the NSE and BSE and reports two businesses: Material Technologies and Biotech.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Material Technologies:** Automotive sealants, Low density underbody coating, Seam sealant that eliminates the need for a separate curing oven, Metal treatment chemicals, High-performance coatings, Engineering adhesives, Electronic adhesives (under development), Battery pack adhesives (under development)
- **Biotech / Biosciences:** Animal feed supplements, Enzymes, Probiotics, Prebiotics, Nutritional products

- New products described as comparable to or more advanced than competitors' offerings - e.g. a low density underbody coating that lets the OEM cut weight and material consumption without performance loss, and a seam sealant that removes the need for a separate curing oven
- Import substitution capability: successfully developed products to replace imports from its erstwhile US-based technical partner, ND Industries, Inc.

- Internationally certified quality systems (ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, IATF 16949, FAMI-QS) supporting OEM qualification

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen product development activities, improve manufacturing efficiencies, attain increasing quality standards and develop new technologies to sustain in a competitive market
- Sustain a higher-than-proportionate R&D spend over the medium term - management calls it possibly the only way to outgrow the competition - after establishing a new product development centre for sealants, adhesives and coatings at Alandi and upgrading the metal treatment chemicals laboratories at the Mahape head office
- Drive sealants growth through technology-led new products that match or exceed competitor offerings (low density underbody coating enabling OEM weight/material reduction; seam sealant that eliminates a separate curing oven), with more such breakthroughs in the pipeline to win additional Indian and multinational OEM customers
- Expand the Engineering Adhesives product range into electronic adhesives and battery pack adhesives as a strategic entry into electronic components and battery packs for EVs and electricity storage
- Import substitution - develop in-house products to replace imports from erstwhile US-based technical partner ND Industries, Inc.
- Expand the Metal Treatment Chemicals footprint across all sub-segments and across the country
- Cost optimization, quality benchmarking and investment in newer product technologies as key focus areas across all divisions of Material Technologies
- Grow the animal health and nutrition (Biotech) business through seasonal campaigns, customer engagement, brand-building (webinars, nukkad meetings) and new product introductions
- Recover margin by passing through elevated raw material costs to customers, which management says customers are accepting with a lag
- Continue investing in people and digital systems - structured leadership development programmes, customised development journeys for high-potential talent, and HR systems upgrades - alongside SAP S/4HANA-based control and reporting
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company's disclosed expansion in FY26 was R&D and capability build-out rather than manufacturing capacity addition. In FY26 a new product development centre for sealants, adhesives and coatings was established at Alandi at a cost of over Rs 5 crore, covering infrastructure and state-of-the-art instrumentation, and now employs 14 scientists, engineers and chemists, up from 8 last year. The laboratories for metal treatment chemicals at the head office in Mahape are also being upgraded, and management says such higher-than-proportionate R&D investment will continue in the medium term. On the commercial side, the Metal Treatment Chemicals business expanded its footprint across all sub-segments and across the country; Engineering Adhesives is expanding its product range into electronic adhesives and battery pack adhesives for a strategic entry into electronic components and battery packs for EVs and electricity storage; and the Company developed products to replace imports from its erstwhile US-based technical partner, ND Industries, Inc. Management also notes that after the demerger the consolidated operating profit margins show it is now able to better absorb existing resources, and that consolidated EBITDA growth came partly from better utilisation of existing resources. No plant-level capacity addition, commissioning timeline or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in the routed text.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Continued growth of the Indian economy and higher consumption driven by economic stability, moderate inflation and the demographic dividend; India's GDP grew by 7.7%, the highest again among major economies, with inflation within the RBI's target band
- Growth of the Indian automotive industry and increasing adoption of advanced sealing technologies
- Large-scale expansion projects in the Indian steel industry leading to more demand for treatment solutions and environment-friendly chemistries
- Increasing penetration of white goods in India, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring countries
- Rising per capita protein consumption and a shift from vegetarian to flexitarian diets, giving an opportunity to increase the animal health and nutrition business
- Indian chemical industry, estimated at around US$250 billion, expected to grow to nearly US$300 billion by 2028, supported by capacity expansions, export opportunities, sustainability-focused products and government initiatives (source: IBEF); specialty chemicals remains the key growth driver
- Indian animal health market valued at Rs 92.62 billion in 2025 and projected to reach Rs 171.91 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 7.11% (source: IMARC), driven by government initiatives, better veterinary infrastructure, preventive healthcare awareness, commercial livestock expansion, pet ownership and the 'One Health' approach
- Demand for high-quality animal feed supplements likely to remain strong on rising population, changing dietary preferences and focus on sustainable and ethical farming
- Margin headwind: a sharp increase in raw material prices from late Q3 onwards, driven by elevated crude oil prices and Middle East geopolitical uncertainty, with customer price increases accepted only with a lag
- Post-demerger operating leverage - management says consolidated operating profit margins show the Company is now able to better absorb the resources after the demerger
- Past investments in technology and people are translating into increased customer acceptance and market penetration
- Threat of intense and price-led competition from global MNCs with larger R&D capabilities and established OEM relationships, as well as from local companies

Almost all of the sealants segment's three-year 30% sales CAGR came from newly introduced products, so a stalled pipeline directly stalls growth.

risks.note: The MD&A states the Company is exposed to safety, health and environmental risks given the diversity and complexity of its industry, and separately lists as a Threat that chemical manufacturing processes are subject to environmental hazards including pollution and waste management issues. one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Chembond Material Technologies Limited, founded in 1975 by Dr. Vinod D. Shah, is a specialty chemicals manufacturer of automotive sealants, adhesives, metal treatment chemicals and high-performance coatings, with an animal health and industrial biotech arm run through subsidiary Chembond …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures specialty chemicals - high performance coatings, automotive sealants, metal treatment chemicals and engineering adhesives - supplying industrial and automotive OEM customers in India and abroad, supported by advanced manufacturing facilities, in-house R&D and internationally certified quality systems. Its subsidiary Chembond Biosciences Limited focuses on animal health and nutrition, producing enzymes, probiotics, prebiotics and nutritional products for the poultry, dairy and aqua segments from modern fermentation and manufacturing facilities. The Company is listed on the NSE and BSE and reports two businesses: Material Technologies and Biotech.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Chembond Biosciences Limited — subsidiary: The Company's only subsidiary, listed in Part A of Form AOC-1 as on March 31, 2026 with reporting currency INR; it is the animal health and nutrition business, producing enzymes, probiotics, prebiotics and nutritional products for the poultry, dairy and aqua segments. Form AOC-1 also records that no subsidiary is yet to commence operations and none was liquidated or sold during the year.
- Visan Trust — related party: The implementing agency through which the Company routed its FY 2025-26 CSR activities. The routed text names it only as the CSR channel and does not state any shareholding, control or related-party relationship.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Material Technologies:** Automotive sealants, Low density underbody coating, Seam sealant that eliminates the need for a separate curing oven, Metal treatment chemicals, High-performance coatings, Engineering adhesives, Electronic adhesives (under development), Battery pack adhesives (under development)
- **Biotech / Biosciences:** Animal feed supplements, Enzymes, Probiotics, Prebiotics, Nutritional products

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Automotive OEMs (Indian and multinational)
- Steel industry (metal treatment solutions)
- White goods
- Electronic components
- Battery packs for EVs and electricity storage
- Poultry
- Dairy
- Aqua / aquaculture
- India (domestic demand across diversified sectors); white goods penetration in the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring countries

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Continued growth of the Indian economy and higher consumption driven by economic stability, moderate inflation and the demographic dividend; India's GDP grew by 7.7%, the highest again among major economies, with inflation within the RBI's target band
- Growth of the Indian automotive industry and increasing adoption of advanced sealing technologies
- Large-scale expansion projects in the Indian steel industry leading to more demand for treatment solutions and environment-friendly chemistries
- Increasing penetration of white goods in India, the Indian subcontinent and neighbouring countries
- Rising per capita protein consumption and a shift from vegetarian to flexitarian diets, giving an opportunity to increase the animal health and nutrition business
- Indian chemical industry, estimated at around US$250 billion, expected to grow to nearly US$300 billion by 2028, supported by capacity expansions, export opportunities, sustainability-focused products and government initiatives (source: IBEF); specialty chemicals remains the key growth driver
- Indian animal health market valued at Rs 92.62 billion in 2025 and projected to reach Rs 171.91 billion by 2034, a CAGR of 7.11% (source: IMARC), driven by government initiatives, better veterinary infrastructure, preventive healthcare awareness, commercial livestock expansion, pet ownership and the 'One Health' approach
- Demand for high-quality animal feed supplements likely to remain strong on rising population, changing dietary preferences and focus on sustainable and ethical farming
- Margin headwind: a sharp increase in raw material prices from late Q3 onwards, driven by elevated crude oil prices and Middle East geopolitical uncertainty, with customer price increases accepted only with a lag
- Post-demerger operating leverage - management says consolidated operating profit margins show the Company is now able to better absorb the resources after the demerger
- Past investments in technology and people are translating into increased customer acceptance and market penetration
- Threat of intense and price-led competition from global MNCs with larger R&D capabilities and established OEM relationships, as well as from local companies

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Strengthen product development activities, improve manufacturing efficiencies, attain increasing quality standards and develop new technologies to sustain in a competitive market
- Sustain a higher-than-proportionate R&D spend over the medium term - management calls it possibly the only way to outgrow the competition - after establishing a new product development centre for sealants, adhesives and coatings at Alandi and upgrading the metal treatment chemicals laboratories at the Mahape head office
- Drive sealants growth through technology-led new products that match or exceed competitor offerings (low density underbody coating enabling OEM weight/material reduction; seam sealant that eliminates a separate curing oven), with more such breakthroughs in the pipeline to win additional Indian and multinational OEM customers
- Expand the Engineering Adhesives product range into electronic adhesives and battery pack adhesives as a strategic entry into electronic components and battery packs for EVs and electricity storage
- Import substitution - develop in-house products to replace imports from erstwhile US-based technical partner ND Industries, Inc.
- Expand the Metal Treatment Chemicals footprint across all sub-segments and across the country
- Cost optimization, quality benchmarking and investment in newer product technologies as key focus areas across all divisions of Material Technologies
- Grow the animal health and nutrition (Biotech) business through seasonal campaigns, customer engagement, brand-building (webinars, nukkad meetings) and new product introductions
- Recover margin by passing through elevated raw material costs to customers, which management says customers are accepting with a lag
- Continue investing in people and digital systems - structured leadership development programmes, customised development journeys for high-potential talent, and HR systems upgrades - alongside SAP S/4HANA-based control and reporting

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's disclosed expansion in FY26 was R&D and capability build-out rather than manufacturing capacity addition. In FY26 a new product development centre for sealants, adhesives and coatings was established at Alandi at a cost of over Rs 5 crore, covering infrastructure and state-of-the-art instrumentation, and now employs 14 scientists, engineers and chemists, up from 8 last year. The laboratories for metal treatment chemicals at the head office in Mahape are also being upgraded, and management says such higher-than-proportionate R&D investment will continue in the medium term. On the commercial side, the Metal Treatment Chemicals business expanded its footprint across all sub-segments and across the country; Engineering Adhesives is expanding its product range into electronic adhesives and battery pack adhesives for a strategic entry into electronic components and battery packs for EVs and electricity storage; and the Company developed products to replace imports from its erstwhile US-based technical partner, ND Industries, Inc. Management also notes that after the demerger the consolidated operating profit margins show it is now able to better absorb existing resources, and that consolidated EBITDA growth came partly from better utilisation of existing resources. No plant-level capacity addition, commissioning timeline or rupee capex quantum is disclosed in the routed text.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- R&D-led product development: automotive sealants sales have grown at a CAGR of 30% over the last three years, with almost all of that growth from newly introduced products
- New products described as comparable to or more advanced than competitors' offerings - e.g. a low density underbody coating that lets the OEM cut weight and material consumption without performance loss, and a seam sealant that removes the need for a separate curing oven
- Import substitution capability: successfully developed products to replace imports from its erstwhile US-based technical partner, ND Industries, Inc.
- Long-standing customer partnerships and a 51-year operating history (founded 1975), with new customers added and new business won at existing customers in the sealants segment
- Internationally certified quality systems (ISO 9001, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, IATF 16949, FAMI-QS) supporting OEM qualification
- Diversified revenue-generating sources across multiple sectors with strong domestic demand, which management says mitigates macro risk to some extent
- SAP S/4HANA ERP with embedded automated controls and audit trail across data capture, accounting, consolidation and management reporting

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Raw material price volatility and input-cost pass-through lag — The MD&A records a sharp increase in raw material prices from late Q3 onwards which cut over 2 percentage points from product and gross margins, with management stating the bottom line is under stress from elevated input costs because customers accept the necessary price increases only with a lag. Elevated crude oil prices cascade into raw material prices.
- Competition from global MNCs with larger R&D budgets and established OEM relationships — Listed as a Threat in the MD&A. Chembond's growth depends on winning and holding automotive OEM qualifications, where incumbents have deeper R&D capability and existing relationships; the Company's own answer is a higher-than-proportionate R&D spend which it calls possibly the only way to outgrow the competition.

Almost all of the sealants segment's three-year 30% sales CAGR came from newly introduced products, so a stalled pipeline directly stalls growth.
- Safety, health and environmental exposure of chemical manufacturing — The MD&A states the Company is exposed to safety, health and environmental risks given the diversity and complexity of its industry, and separately lists as a Threat that chemical manufacturing processes are subject to environmental hazards including pollution and waste management issues. Mitigation cited: frequent SHE audits, safety training across all locations and a Safety, Health and Environment Policy.
- Geopolitical and supply-chain disruption — Listed as a Threat: economic or geopolitical events such as wars can raise raw material costs or cause delivery delays that create supply chain instability, hitting margins and sales. Management explicitly cites the ongoing Middle East crisis with no clarity on how long it will last, alongside the Russia-Ukraine war.
- Cyberattack risk from industry digitization — Listed as a Threat: digitization of the industry increases the risk of cyberattacks which may lead to data loss, operational disruption and financial loss - relevant given the Company runs SAP S/4HANA as its platform for data capture, accounting, consolidation and management reporting.
- Macro-economic sensitivity - government policy, currency and commodity volatility — The MD&A states that macro-economic conditions such as government policy decisions, currency fluctuations and commodity price volatility can affect the business, partly mitigated because the Company's revenue-generating sources are diversified into various sectors with strong domestic demand.
- Pending litigation against the Company and its Directors — The Board's Report discloses one pending litigation against the Company and its Directors whose order is yet to be received, explained in the Corporate Governance section; apart from this no significant or material order impacting going-concern status was passed by regulators, courts or tribunals.
